headline: Sales edge up, impairment charge sinks quarterly profit
summary_short: Fiscal Q4 net sales rose 2% to $912M, but a $132M intangible-asset impairment and a 34% jump in SG&A drove operating income down 53% to $96M and diluted EPS down 61% to $0.12.
summary_long: Brown-Forman's fiscal Q4 (quarter ended April 30, 2026) net sales rose 2% to $912M (+2% organic), but operating income fell 53% to $96M and diluted EPS fell 61% to $0.12, driven by a $132M non-cash intangible-asset impairment and a 34% rise in SG&A tied to the terminated Pernod Ricard combination talks and higher compensation costs. Gross margin expanded 530bp to 62.6% on favorable acquisition/divestiture and FX effects. For fiscal 2026 overall, net sales fell 1% to $3.9B while free cash flow rose $462M to $893M; the company returned $827M to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. For fiscal 2027, management guided organic net sales approximately flat, organic operating income down 3-5%, and capex of $60-70M.
